nodes.claim: The perfect genetic axiom imports genomes people already have; it never assays.
nodes.detail: An assay pipeline (samples, labs, clinical accreditation) is a different institution, not a harder feature. Consumer raw files (23andMe/AncestryDNA class, hundreds of thousands of genotyped positions) already exist in the hands of exactly the people most likely to bring them, and importing keeps the perfect system on the analysis side, where its comparative advantage (the phenotype battery, gen-3) actually is. Even in the no-practical-limits frame, assaying adds custody and liability without adding analytical power the imported file lacks for trait work.

nodes.claim: In the perfect system the genome stays where the person is; only derived, banded quantities travel.
nodes.detail: Device-side scoring against published weight sets gives the crowd half everything it needs (score bands) while the raw sequence never enters anyone's custody. This is not a privacy compromise on the perfect design — it IS the perfect design, because a genome is unrevokable and familial (gen-6): minimizing custody is minimizing irreversible failure modes, and a system with fewer irreversible failure modes is better on pure design grounds. Open question for a future run: what the ceiling of device-side analysis is (imputation quality without a server, structural variants, polygenic interaction terms).

nodes.claim: The scarce asset is the phenotype battery, not the genotypes; the perfect axiom is designed around that asymmetry.
nodes.detail: Genotypes are commodity files; deep, longitudinal, freely-given phenotypes are what biobanks cannot buy cheaply. InSight's answer corpus is an unusually rich behavioral phenotyping instrument. The perfect genetic axiom therefore optimizes for pairing quality (how many people have BOTH a scored genome and a deep phenotype record) over genotype count, and treats every phenotype-side improvement (questions axiom) as a genetic-axiom improvement. Ranking claim for central: this asymmetry is the genetic axiom's main contribution to the combination. External support arrived with gen-4's scout (2026-08-25): the education–pace-of-aging association in Framingham (DunedinPACE analysis n=3,101, drawn from a three-generation mobility database of n=14,106) holds under within-family sibling fixed effects and across four alternative clocks (Graf 2024, cited at gen-4) — behavioral phenotype carries aging signal that shared family background alone does not explain, which is this asymmetry stated by someone else's data. A future run may raise this node on that basis after full-text verification; note the stronger 'survives polygenic-index adjustment' reading of Graf did NOT survive this run's adversarial check (unconfirmable from the abstract) — the sibling-fixed-effects reading did, and it is the one recorded here. Raised argued→cited 2026-08-27: the instrument premise — that a bank of self-report items is a genetic-grade phenotyping instrument — now has direct external demonstrations. A single well-chosen self-report item carries a genetically valid phenotype at scale: musical beat synchronization, one self-report item in n=606,825, yielded 69 genome-wide-significant loci with SNP-h2 13–16%, and the item was validated against separate experimental rhythm-perception and beat-synchronization measures in independent participants (Niarchou 2022). Web-based participant-driven self-report phenotyping is the founding method of consumer-cohort genetics (Eriksson 2010: 22 self-report traits, ~10,000 participants, novel replicated associations including photic sneeze and asparagus anosmia). Aggregation raises the genetic signal: interest heritability ~32% at item level rises to ~48% at factor and ~53% at superfactor level (Lykken 1993, twin-based) — so the perfect battery scores constructs over many items, which is what a deep answer corpus does by design. And the interests half of the battery is a genuine open frontier, stated precisely after the adversarial pass (which refuted this sentence's first draft): vocational interests are heritable at twin grade (~36% genetic in the combined twin/adoption design of Betsworth 1994; ~36–50% across twin studies), and while NO GWAS of an administered interest INVENTORY (Strong/RIASEC-class) was found, behavioral and educational proxies for interests HAVE been GWASed and show the signal is there — educational-field choice across 463,134 individuals yields 17 genome-wide-significant variants across 7 of 10 fields at mean SNP-h2 ~7%, with signal specific to field choice rather than educational level, and its two recovered latent dimensions (technical-vs-social, practical-vs-abstract) are the axes underlying Holland's RIASEC interest hexagon (Cheesman 2025); STEM occupational choice gives 2 loci at SNP-h2 4.2% (Human Genomics 2023). A deep, inventory-grade interests phenotype paired with imported genotypes would still be first of its kind — and the proxies say it would find something. Provenance note for this rise: the run's environment blocked publisher pages, so sources were verified as real at record grade (consistent title/venue/identifier across independent index records) and figures are snippet-grade unless stated.

nodes.claim: The aging ambition runs through behavior-by-aging-measure crosses over the phenotype battery — the genotype contributes a weak prior, and discovery genetics stays out of scope.
nodes.detail: Scouted and adversarially checked 2026-08-25 (14 refutation searches; fixes applied before landing — see LOG). Provenance, per figure: sources were verified to exist via multiple independent indexes; the skeptic pass then confirmed against source-side text the 0.47% GrimAge instrument strength (4 SNPs), MIMOSA's 0.20 average imputation correlation, Timmers' ~5-year decile gap, Graf's n=3,101 analysis / n=14,106 database, and TruDiagnostic's n=14,213; the 4.41% upper instrument figure remains abstract-grade pending full text. Three findings ground the restated claim. (1) The genotype file's own aging signal is a weak prior: longevity GWAS are dominated by APOE (Deelen 2019); the parental-lifespan PGS separates extreme deciles by roughly five years of mean lifespan — a population-decile contrast, not an individual prediction (Timmers 2019); genome-wide-significant SNP instruments for epigenetic age acceleration explain 0.47%–4.41% of the respective clock's variance (4 SNPs for GrimAge; Morales Berstein 2022 over the Gibson 2019 / McCartney 2021 GWAS). That is an instrument-strength figure, not a polygenic-score ceiling — a genome-wide PGS would explain more, and its ceiling is not established here — but the ordering still cautions: GrimAge, the strongest mortality predictor among the clocks, is the least genetically instrumentable. The heritability ceiling of longevity is itself contested across a 5x range — below 10% once assortative mating is modeled (Ruby 2018), up to ~50% for intrinsic lifespan once extrinsic mortality is corrected (Shenhar 2026, itself already challenged in preprint: bioRxiv 2026.04.02.716222) — and the distinction that survives every branch of that dispute is that heritability is not predictability from a common-SNP array: even at h2~50%, a consumer file's realized predictive power is bounded by common-variant tagging. So the genotype yields a legitimate low-resolution prior, never a measurement (gen-7). (2) Discovery stays out of scope, on the cited studies' own designs: the longevity/lifespan/healthspan GWAS above ran at n≈300k–1M (Timmers 2019, Zenin 2019); an app-scale paired cohort does not play that game. The product's own pricing agrees (AXES-PLAN §4 on main) — internal context, not external evidence, and marked as such. (3) The valuable cross is established science, not speculation: educational mobility predicts DunedinPACE pace-of-aging and mortality (analysis n=3,101 with methylation data, from a three-generation n=14,106 mobility database), holding under within-family sibling fixed effects and across four alternative clocks (Graf 2024); conscientiousness tracks slower second/third-generation clock aging across cohorts totalling N>6,000 (Stephan 2025); psychosocioeconomic stress and status associate with GrimAge/DunedinPACE acceleration (PMID 38824837). What the perfect axiom therefore contributes to aging research: the deepest behavioral phenotype battery crossed with imported aging measurements (gen-8) and genotype priors (gen-7), generating behavior-aging correlates worth handing to real research — literature-grounded hypothesis work over consented aggregates, never medical advice (charter §9). Edge change this run: the dependency on gen-5 (LLM sequence models) was dropped on ladder grounds — a cited node depending on a conjecture is evidence flowing uphill; the ambition's real dependencies are the boundary (gen-7) and the import door (gen-8).

nodes.claim: LLM-shaped sequence models are the annotation engine of the perfect genetic analysis layer, not its individual-prediction engine: they supply variant-effect, rare-variant and fine-mapping priors that feed an additive polygenic layer, which remains the auditable predictor.
nodes.detail: Rewritten and raised conjecture→cited 2026-08-27, answering central's 2026-08-26 question (the decisive comparison against a tuned polygenic-score baseline). The comparison has an answer, narrowed by the adversarial pass from a universal negative to what the evidence licenses. (1) No INDEPENDENTLY REPLICATED demonstration exists — searched under five framings across publisher, preprint and index sources, Aug 2026 — of a sequence model predicting a complex human trait at individual level better than a tuned PGS. The one published claim to the contrary is Epi-PRS (Zeng, Guo, Liu & Wong, PNAS 2025): a genomic sequence model imputes personal epigenomic features as genotype–phenotype intermediates, and the record reports ~11–12% higher AUC than named tuned baselines (LDpred2, PRS-CS) for breast cancer and T2D in UK Biobank. No independent replication was found — and the same record reports that non-LLM nonlinear baselines (Genotype-GBRT, Genotype-PCA-GBRT) ALSO beat LDpred2/PRS-CS at large n in that study, so the demonstrated gain is plausibly nonlinearity plus rare-variant reach rather than the sequence model as such. Aside from that unreplicated result, the models' documented strengths are variant-effect and pathogenicity prediction, regulatory annotation and molecular phenotypes (Nucleotide Transformer; Evo; Borzoi), and an independent benchmark finds DNA foundation models competitive on pathogenic-variant identification but weaker than specialized models on expression and causal-QTL tasks (Feng 2025). (2) At the individual level the failure is measured, not suspected: the companion Nature Genetics 2023 papers show sequence-to-function models poorly explain inter-individual expression variation, with cross-individual correlations centered near zero and effect directions frequently wrong (Sasse 2023: of 184 genes with known causal variants, Enformer predictions were anti-correlated for roughly 43% — snippet-grade figure; Huang 2023: independent cohort, same conclusion). The 2025–2026 generation improved, not solved, this: AlphaGenome raises direction-of-effect odds (OR ~3.0, Shen 2025 — preprint, snippet-grade), approaches the heritability ceiling for chromatin-accessibility variation while remaining far below it for gene expression (2026 modality-gap preprint), and a 2026 review still concludes deep models face significant challenges outperforming linear models for cross-individual expression prediction (Dubey & Shen 2026). (3) The structural bound, which is the load-bearing half of the claim: common-variant genetic variance for complex traits is predominantly additive — argued from theory and data (Hill, Goddard & Visscher 2008: high additive share expected under U-shaped allele-frequency distributions regardless of gene-level dominance or epistasis) and directly measured at biobank scale (Hivert 2021: 70 traits, 254,679 unrelated individuals; average variance shares — additive 0.208 of phenotypic, dominance 0.001, epistatic 0.055 — snippet-grade triple; the authors conclude epistasis has a limited role and is unlikely to explain a substantial fraction of missing heritability). Whatever nonlinearity exists at gene level, the population-level variance a predictor can exploit is predominantly additive — dominance negligible, the epistatic share minor — so a linear score captures most of the common-variant ceiling by construction; this is not a capability gap that closes with model scale, it bounds the headroom (without zeroing it, which is exactly the crack the Epi-PRS/GBRT results in (1) sit in). Consistent with the bound: deep nets did not beat linear models on ~100,000 UK Biobank individuals (Bellot 2018 — the title asks the question and the answer is no); reported nonlinear gains are relative gains on small absolute bases with the PRS retained as a feature (Elgart 2022); an 80-phenotype end-to-end benchmark reports PGS workflows winning a majority with a large fraction of practical ties (counts unconfirmed at record grade; the same benchmark reports PRS-tool failure modes too — PRSice instability, lassosum collapse on 13 phenotypes — so it is no clean sweep; small self-report cohort, stress-test grade). (4) Where the models DO belong in the perfect layer: as the annotation engine. Functional annotations improve additive PGS while the predictor stays Bayesian-linear (SBayesRC: +14% within-ancestry and up to +34% cross-ancestry accuracy — Zheng 2024); functionally-informed fine-mapping localizes causal variants better (PolyFun, Weissbrod 2020) and sequence-model priors add further (+9.45% additional fine-mapped variants at PIP>0.8 — Borzoi-informed Sniff, 2025 preprint); protein language models raise rare-variant association-discovery yield (AlphaMissense, Cheng 2023; ESM-class burden scoring, Cell Genomics 2025) — discovery power, explicitly not individual predictive accuracy. (5) This division of labor strengthens gen-2: an additive score over published weight sets is exactly what a device can compute, so keeping prediction on-device costs nothing predictive — the heavy models live on the public annotation side, inside the published weights and priors, never on the per-person path. It is also the genetic-domain instance of pat-6's law: the tuned classical baseline holds below the data-volume crossover — and in genomics no independently replicated crossing has been published; Epi-PRS is the one candidate, unresolved. pat-6's own text records gen-5's question as open, and this run answers it in exactly that qualified form. (6) The Epi-PRS wildcard from (1) is the named scout task: open the paper from an unblocked network — exact deltas, baseline tuning details, and any replication or critique since; two adjacent preprint-grade items to sweep with it (arXiv 2509.20702, embedding-augmented risk prediction; GENPHIRE, medRxiv 2025). If the gain replicates AND is attributable to the sequence model specifically rather than to nonlinearity, this node's claim widens from 'annotation engine' to 'annotation plus epigenomic-intermediate imputation'; the two-layer architecture — auditable additive predictor, heavy models on the public annotation side — survives either way. Provenance: publisher pages egress-blocked this run; sources record-verified via independent index records; figures snippet-grade unless stated. Edge changes this run: the pat-1 edge was dropped (after the rewrite this node no longer argues for learned sequence representations as the engine; the shared content — a classical auditable baseline that the learned layer must beat — now runs through pat-6) and supports-edges to gen-2 and pat-6 were added. Cross-graph hygiene flagged for the optimizer and pattern lanes (LOG row): pat-1 still carries a refines edge to gen-5 justified by the pre-rewrite claim, and pat-6→gen-5 refines plus the new gen-5→pat-6 supports now form a mutual pair.

nodes.claim: Genetic data is never about one person; the perfect consent model is familial-aware.
nodes.detail: A genome is shared with relatives who never consented. The perfect system therefore publishes only aggregate couplings (never an individual's genetic readout to anyone else), states the kinship fact in consent copy, and treats 'who participates' as itself confidential. This is a design axiom under CHARTER §9, not a limitation to engineer around.

nodes.claim: A SNP genotype file carries a prior on aging, never a measurement of it — the boundary is what the assay reads, not statistics.
nodes.detail: Added by the 2026-08-25 scout; adversarially checked the same run (the check narrowed this node — see below). Every epigenetic clock — Horvath 2013 and Hannum 2013 (first generation, trained on chronological age), PhenoAge 2018 and GrimAge 2019 (second, trained on mortality/morbidity), DunedinPACE 2022 (third, pace of aging) — consumes CpG methylation values from a dedicated methylation array (Illumina 450K/EPIC class). The newest strong aging measures consume plasma proteomics instead: ~200 of ~2,900 Olink proteins predict chronological age at r~0.94 in UK Biobank with external validation (Argentieri 2024), and organ-specific plasma signatures track per-organ aging and disease (Oh 2023). A consumer genotyping array cannot report CpG methylation state: 5mC reads as C to the assay chemistry (amplification erases the mark, but even native DNA reads identically — amplification is sufficient for the loss, not fundamental to it), and the array's probe content interrogates genotype, not methylation. The boundary is probe content and the absent methylation channel, NOT bisulfite chemistry alone: Infinium signal on non-bisulfite-converted DNA still carries some age signal through non-methylation factors ('pseudomethylation', Porter 2025), so the precise claim is that no methylation clock is computable from a 23andMe-class genotype CALL file — the methylation channel is simply absent from it; whether age-correlated signal could be scraped from raw array intensities is a different question about a different input, which consumers do not hold. Imputing methylation from mQTLs does not cross the boundary either: prediction models average a correlation of ~0.20 per CpG (MIMOSA, preprint-grade), and what they recover is by construction the genetic component alone — a polygenic score wearing a clock's costume, discarding exactly the environmental and stochastic signal that makes clocks informative. The adversarial pass hunted for a counterexample (any published method computing a genuine methylation clock from SNP-array genotype data) and found none. So 'what can the genome say about aging' has an architectural answer: the imported genotype supplies a fixed, weak prior (gen-4's figures); the measurement of how a person is actually aging lives in other assays, which the import principle can reach (gen-8) but the genotype file cannot. This sharpens gen-1: 'import, never assay' is not a limitation on the aging ambition, because the thing an assay would add — a clock reading — is itself importable (gen-8).

nodes.claim: The import principle generalizes: the perfect axiom imports any molecular self-measurement the person already holds — consumer methylation files first among them.
nodes.detail: Added by the 2026-08-25 scout; adversarially checked the same run (the check inverted one claim here — see custody paragraph). gen-1's argument was written about genotype files, but its logic — stay on the analysis side, import what consented people already hold — reaches further, and the aging half of the theory needs it to (gen-7: the aging measurement is not in the genotype file). The enabling premise is peer-reviewed fact: consumer-platform methylation cohorts are publication-grade — a TruDiagnostic consumer cohort of n=14,213 serves as a validation cohort in Nature Aging (Chen & Dwaraka 2026, alongside Generation Scotland n=18,672), and the same platform ran a randomized twin diet trial with epigenetic-clock outcomes in BMC Medicine (Dwaraka 2024). The market detail is vendor-grade and labeled so in sources: TruDiagnostic, Elysium Index and myDNAge sell EPIC-class methylation testing to consumers, and TruDiagnostic states customers can download raw data (>850k CpG loci, IDATs on request) — so raw-file import is reported-possible at vendor grade, to be confirmed at vendor-ToS or peer-review grade before gen-2's device-side story is extended to methylation. Given that, actual clock measurements can enter the perfect system by the same door genotypes do; the axiom still never assays. Two consequences. (a) Methylation is a STATE measurement where genotype is a constant, so the perfect import is a longitudinal series of files, not one file — repeat imports are first-class as a property of what the system ACCEPTS from people who already hold such data; per charter §9 this is never a suggestion that anyone test, re-test, or intervene on a schedule — the axiom describes an import door, not a protocol. (b) Custody and consent carry over at FULL strength, not reduced: a methylation array file is also a genotype file at reduced density — genotypes at thousands of SNPs are recoverable from Infinium EPIC data at >98% concordance, enough to identify hundreds of close-relative pairs in a research cohort (MethylGenotyper 2024), and EPIC arrays carry dedicated identity probes — so gen-6's familial-consent logic and gen-2's custody minimization apply to imported methylation files exactly as to genomes.

nodes.claim: Traits the other axioms measure map onto genetic architecture — heritability, polygenicity, effect-size distribution, functional enrichment, correlation structure — not onto gene lists: for psychological and preference traits, 'which genes' has a distribution as its answer.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27, answering the first half of the owner's 2026-08-25 cross-connection question (QUESTIONS.md): how do traits the other axioms measure map onto specific genes? For psychological and preference traits the honest answer is a distribution, not a list. The fourth law of behavior genetics is exactly this claim — a typical behavioral trait is associated with very many variants, each accounting for a very small share of variability (Chabris 2015) — and the omnigenic model gives it a mechanism: interconnected regulatory networks spread heritability across essentially all genes expressed in trait-relevant cells (Boyle 2017; contested in degree but not in polygenicity by Wray 2018; O'Connor 2019 adds the evolutionary why — negative selection purges large effects at critical genes, flattening the effect-size distribution). Twin-scale baseline: across 17,804 traits from fifty years of twin studies, mean reported heritability is ~49% and most traits are consistent with additive-only models (Polderman 2015). The measured shape, per axis-relevant trait: cognitive ability — n=269,867 gives 205 loci, SNP-h2 ~19%, and a polygenic score explaining 4.81% in independent cohorts (Savage 2018); educational attainment — n≈3M gives 3,952 lead SNPs and a PGI predicting 12–16% (Okbay 2022); neuroticism — n=449,484 gives 136 loci (Nagel 2018; the later MVP-led analysis reports 158, Gupta 2024); the other Big Five stood at 2–14 genome-wide-significant loci each as late as 2024 (extraversion 14, agreeableness 3, conscientiousness 2, openness 7 — Gupta 2024) before a 611k–1.14M-sample analysis found 1,257 lead variants with SNP-h2 4.8–9.3%, or 10.5–16.2% corrected for measurement unreliability (ReGPC 2025 — preprint-grade). The saturated contrast case: height, at n=5.4M, needed 12,111 SNPs spread over ~7,209 segments covering ~21% of the genome to capture ~40% of phenotypic variance — and only in European ancestry, 10–20% elsewhere (Yengo 2022). Even the most genetically tractable physical trait saturates to a genome-wide distribution with ancestry-conditional coverage; perfect capability yields a distribution over the genome, never a map of named genes. The gene-list alternative has a documented failure record, not merely an absence of success: 18 historical depression candidate genes performed no better than non-candidate genes across large samples (Border 2019); 1 of 32 replication tests across 12 IQ candidate genes reached even nominal significance (Chabris 2012); and FOXP2's human-specific selection story dissolved as a sample-composition artifact (Atkinson 2018) — while the KE-family FOXP2 mutation stands, which is the right lesson: monogenic DISORDERS of behavior exist; monogenic variation in normal-range traits is what does not. The one honest counterexample class is the pleiotropic hub: CADM2 associates with ~50 behavioral traits from risk-taking to diet (UK Biobank phenome-wide scan, PMID 35867259; Arends 2021) — nameable and mechanistically interpretable, but a hub of a behavioral cluster is a feature OF the architecture (a high-centrality node in the coupling structure), not a gene for a trait. What the perfect cross-connection therefore delivers per trait: an architecture vector — SNP-heritability, polygenicity and effect-size-distribution parameters, functional and cell-type enrichment (stratified LD-score partitioning, Finucane 2015; e.g. intelligence signal concentrating in striatal medium spiny and hippocampal pyramidal neurons, Savage 2018; neuroticism in dopaminergic and serotonergic lineages, Nagel 2018), and the trait's position in genetic-correlation structure (gen-11) — plus the short exception list where a named gene genuinely carries the signal (gen-10). Cell-type and tissue enrichment is itself cross-axis content: it maps question- and test-measured traits onto the body axiom's organs and cell populations without any individual-level data changing hands. nodes.claim: Named genes carry cross-axis signal only where a trait is the direct output of a single protein — a percept, a pigment, a secretion; downstream of a mild hedonic percept the signal collapses toward preference and behavior, while aversive toxic percepts carry it through.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27, the second half of the owner's cross-connection answer: where 'specific genes' IS the literal truth. The boundary was sharpened twice by the adversarial pass. It is not 'sensory traits' as a class, and not 'percepts' either (the first draft said percepts, and its own case list violated that — earwax, eye color and hair color are not percepts): it is single-protein DIRECT-OUTPUT phenotypes — traits that are the immediate output of one receptor, enzyme, transporter or regulatory element, whether that output is a percept, a pigment or a secretion. The clean cases: OR5A1 rs6591536 explains >96% of β-ionone odor-sensitivity variation — functionally Mendelian — and flips the odor's reported quality from floral to pungent (Jaeger 2013); ABCC11 rs17822931 determines earwax type outright (Yoshiura 2006); a three-SNP OCA2 intron-1 haplotype explains ~74% of blue/non-blue eye-color variation (Duffy 2007), and the single SNP rs12913832 in HERC2 predicts eye color at ordinal R2 ≈ 0.68, with CC genotypes at ~1% probability of brown eyes (Sturm 2008) — European-cohort quantities, since eye-color variance is itself near-absent in most non-European populations; TAS2R38 PAV/AVI haplotypes explain ~75–80% (source-dependent) of PTC/PROP bitterness perception (Kim 2003); ALDH2 rs671 dominates alcohol flush in East Asian cohorts (association P values down to <1e-4740 reported across GWAS — Science Advances 2023; flushing SNP-h2 ~13% roughly halving to ~6% conditioned on the lead variants — Cho 2023), with rs671 essentially absent outside East Asia; LCT/MCM6 rs4988235 is near-deterministic for adult lactase persistence in Europeans (though NOT for how much dairy anyone consumes — no variance figure for intake is citable); and OR7D4 haplotypes alter androstenone odor perception and valence (Keller 2007 — no numeric variance share citable). The whole exception list is ancestry-conditional in both allele frequency and trait variance — the point gen-9 makes structurally applies here case by case. Downstream of the percept, the fate of the signal splits, and the split is itself lawful. For MILD, HEDONIC percepts the signal collapses on the way to preference and behavior: TAS2R38 genotype→percept is near-Mendelian, but a 72-study systematic review finds bitter-taster status minimally associated with actual food preference and intake — pooled associations small and non-significant across food groups, one modest exception (carbohydrate intake, dz=−0.14; Nutrition Research 2025, PROSPERO CRD42024587607); cilantro soap-taste, the popular 'gene for' story, is really a weak-effect locus — rs72921001 at OR 0.81 per allele with common-SNP h2 ≈0.087, OR6A2 a plausible receptor candidate, never demonstrated causal (Eriksson 2012); MC1R, the textbook red-hair gene, explains only ~73% of red-hair SNP-heritability and most two-variant carriers are not redheads (Morgan 2018); chronotype is decisively polygenic — 351 loci at n=697,828, SNP-h2 ~13.7%, with the top vs bottom 5% of morningness alleles differing by ~25 minutes of accelerometer-measured sleep timing (Jones 2019); habitual coffee intake is polygenic with two interpretable pharmacogenes (CYP1A2, AHR) riding on top (Cornelis 2015), its genetic correlations cohort-dependent (cited at gen-11). But for AVERSIVE, TOXIC percepts the signal carries through to behavior: ALDH2 rs671 is described in the literature as the major genetic determinant of alcohol CONSUMPTION in East Asians — the acetaldehyde flush is punishing enough that the percept-level effect survives into the behavioral phenotype (a similar pattern is reported for CYP2A6 and smoking quantity — noted, not source-verified this run). The adversarial pass supplied this split after catching the first draft asserting collapse and citing ALDH2-on-consumption in the same paragraph; the repaired boundary is predictive rather than descriptive: expect gene-level signal in a behavior only when the intervening percept is aversive enough to dominate hedonic and social modulation. The consequence for the cross-connection: of everything the question, test, body and interest axioms measure, there is a small, enumerable set of items where a genotype genuinely predicts the individual answer — items that ask about the direct output itself (does cilantro taste soapy; how bitter is this; do you flush when drinking; can you smell asparagus metabolites in urine) — and a large remainder where the genome contributes architecture and priors only (gen-9). The perfect axiom knows which side of the boundary each of its crosses sits on and prices the cross accordingly: direct-output items are the highest-value per-genotype pairing anchors the phenotype battery can hold, everything else is population-level architecture. This sharpens que-1 from the genetic side — a bank that wants genetic tractability includes direct-output items on the shared spine (REQUESTS row this run). nodes.claim: A population-level gene–trait coupling is a composite; the perfect cross-connection publishes every coupling with its decomposition — direct effect, genetic nurture, mating structure — because the split is real, measurable, and trait-specific.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27, the third piece of the cross-connection answer: what a gene–trait coupling honestly IS once measured. Four measured facts force the decomposition. (1) For attainment-type traits, a large share of the population-level signal is not a direct genetic effect on the person: the polygenic score built from parents' NON-transmitted alleles carries ~30% of the transmitted score's association with educational attainment (genetic nurture — Kong 2018, 29.9% snippet-grade); within-sibship estimates shrink for EA, cognitive ability and others, with EA SNP-h2 falling 0.13→0.04 within siblings, a 76% attenuation (Howe 2022: 178,086 siblings, 25 phenotypes — snippet-grade figures); EA4's direct effects are roughly half the population PGI association (Okbay 2022); and occupational-status prediction drops 54–57% within families, decomposed as 22–27% indirect parental effects plus 21–27% assortative mating (Akimova 2024). (2) The split is trait-specific, not a law — and for personality it is genuinely unsettled, which the node records rather than resolves: the largest within-family personality analysis (611k–1.14M population, 51k within-family) reports no identifiable within-family reduction in Big Five prediction and minimal confounding from stratification, dynastic effects or assortative mating (ReGPC 2025 — preprint-grade), while a smaller peer-reviewed twin analysis found within-family neuroticism PGS prediction reduced by 80.4% relative to between-family in up to 2,366 DZ pairs (Selzam 2019 — peer-reviewed but with wide uncertainty at that n, and the gap largely closed after adjusting for socioeconomic status). The honest current reading: attainment traits are demonstrably the heavily-confounded class across multiple designs; for personality the biggest data says clean and a smaller peer-reviewed result says otherwise — the perfect system carries the tension as data. Either way, a system that showed one shrinkage number for 'genetics' would be wrong in several directions at once. (3) The genome's connective tissue across traits — genetic-correlation structure (the atlas method, Bulik-Sullivan 2015: 276 correlations among 24 traits from summary statistics alone; joint factor models over that structure, Grotzinger 2019; risk tolerance sharing lead loci with drinking, smoking, speeding and sexual-behavior phenotypes at 46 of 99 loci, Karlsson Linnér 2019; occupational status at rg 0.96–0.97 with educational attainment, Akimova 2024) — is genuinely cross-axis content: it couples traits measured by different instruments at the latent genetic level, computable from published summary statistics without any individual-level data changing hands. But it is partly mating-market artifact: cross-mate phenotypic correlations predict genetic-correlation estimates at R2=74%, and some reported psychiatric rg values are congruent with cross-trait assortative mating alone (Border 2022, Science); the EA–BMI genetic correlation attenuates toward zero within siblings (Howe 2022); and assortative mating biases marker-based heritability estimates themselves (Border 2022, Nature Communications). (4) The coupling also depends on the measurement: the same self-reported coffee-intake phenotype produced genetic correlations with cognition and psychiatric traits that flipped sign or vanished between 23andMe and UK Biobank (2024 GWAS comparison) — ascertainment and item wording change the genetic answer, which binds this axiom's couplings to the questions axiom's measurement discipline and is a direct, citable warning for any self-report-derived phenotype. Consequence: in the perfect system a cross-axis genetic coupling is never published as a bare correlation. It is a decomposed quantity — direct, genetic-nurture and mating-structure components, with a within-family evidence grade and cohort/measurement provenance attached — because whether a coupling is biology or social structure is itself first-class data, and the difference is measurable. This is the honesty constraint on cen-1's shared latent space: genetic coordinates carry decomposition labels or they mislead every axiom they touch.
